audit_findings.title: Gross cash add-back may double count customer advances
audit_findings.magnitude: $3,110.6 million gross cash/STI add-back ($7.85 per share; 12.3% of base equity value), versus $3,756.3 million of current and noncurrent deferred revenue and a $1,822.7 million first-half 2026 deferred-revenue inflow
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments while OE benefits from customer-funded working-capital inflows, without reserving cash needed to satisfy the associated performance obligations or operate the business.
audit_findings.evidence: Payments received in advance for service arrangements or product delivery are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized in net sales when the revenue recognition criteria are met.
audit_findings.explanation: The demonstrated error is treating the entire $3,110.6 million balance as excess cash without an excess-cash analysis. The amount actually restricted economically by customer obligations is unresolved, so the full add-back is not necessarily wrong dollar-for-dollar. Nevertheless, the exposed bridge amount is large enough to materially affect every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash to contract liabilities, expected fulfillment spending, restricted cash, acquisition funding and minimum operating cash; normalize customer-advance working-capital benefits in OE and rerun using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The disclosed capex step-up is absent from the projected OE path
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 guidance of $550-$570 million is $323.6-$343.6 million above 2025 capex of $226.4 million, equal to 20.5%-21.7% of the $1,582.3 million OE anchor; first-half 2026 spending was already $288.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is projected directly from a 2025 anchor that deducts substantially lower capex, while the modeled growth and operating capacity require additional investment.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to have capital expenditures (including capitalized software) of $425 to $525 in 2026 in order to support capacity expansion across the business.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted step-up is demonstrated by the projection method and the latest filed guidance. Whether every incremental dollar is recurring maintenance or growth investment remains unresolved, but its scale relative to anchor OE makes it reasonably capable of changing intrinsic value materially.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $550-$570 million program between maintenance, replacement and growth capex; establish the continuing reinvestment required for each growth scenario and rerun the OE paths accordingly.

audit_findings.title: The OE numerator and valuation-date perimeter are mismatched
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation combines FY2025 OE with June/July 2026 cash, debt and shares after five completed acquisitions, so the numerator does not represent the businesses supporting the valuation-date capital claims and bridge.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: PurgeRite contributed less than one month to FY2025, Great Lakes contributed only a partial year, and three additional businesses closed in 2026. The filing identifies $226.3 million of first-half 2026 acquisition-related sales and $331.8 million of consideration for the three 2026 acquisitions, but does not provide enough acquired OE to quantify the value effect or establish its direction. The mismatch is material because acquisition costs are reflected while full-period operating economics are not.
audit_findings.action: Build valuation-date trailing-twelve-month or pro forma OE for Great Lakes, PurgeRite, BMarko Structures, Strategic Thermal Labs and ThermoKey, excluding pending Utility Innovation, then rerun all scenarios with the same-date bridge and share count.

audit_findings.title: PurgeRite contingent consideration is an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $206.1 million latest filed PurgeRite liability ($0.52 per share; 0.81% of base equity value), with $250.0 million maximum exposure ($0.63 per share; 0.99% of base equity value)
audit_findings.mechanism: An acquisition-related cash claim is omitted from the equity bridge and is not extinguished through ordinary interest expense retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is required to pay up to $ 250.0 of additional cash consideration if PurgeRite achieves certain post-closing performance metrics, pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Acquisition Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated, and the latest liability is higher than the $144.1 million year-end amount. However, even the contractual maximum is less than 1% of the $25,342 million base equity value and would reduce base value per share only from $63.92 to about $63.29, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the latest expected PurgeRite liability from the bridge, or explicitly model its settlement in OE, while preventing double counting of the $62.0 million first-half 2026 fair-value loss.

audit_findings.title: Earned performance awards are missing from the share ceiling
audit_findings.mechanism: Earned awards that will convert into RSUs and common shares increase the fully diluted denominator, reducing value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of stock distributed will vary based on the company-based metric achieved in each fiscal year and the future price of the shares.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that the 2023-2025 performance metrics were achieved and settlement will vary with the future share price. The supplied share ceiling reportedly excludes these awards, but neither the earned dollar value, conversion price nor non-duplicative share count is established. Dilution therefore exists as an unresolved possibility whose materiality cannot be determined from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the award schedules and accrued earned values, calculate shares at the contractual conversion dates under target and maximum outcomes, reconcile them to reported RSUs and diluted EPS shares, and rerun value per share with the non-duplicative amount.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded pension obligation may require a bridge deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $76.5 million year-end 2025 net pension liability ($0.19 per share; 0.30% of base equity value)
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual unfunded employee-benefit claim not captured through future OE would reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The projected benefit obligation for all plans was $ 93.4 and $ 74.0 at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and the net liability recognized to the balance sheet was $ 76.5 and $ 62.3 at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether a separate deduction is required remains unresolved because future pension expense and contributions may already capture part of the obligation. Even deducting the entire filed net liability would reduce base value per share only from $63.92 to about $63.73 and represents 0.30% of base equity value, which is not material to the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the latest funded status, plan assets, expected contributions and pension costs included in OE; deduct only the residual amount not otherwise modeled.
